name: Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum

criteria.description: Characteristic yellowish papular skin lesions with peau d’orange texture, typically on the neck and flexural areas
Angioid streaks and peau d’orange fundus changes on ophthalmologic examination
Calcification and fragmentation of elastic fibers in skin biopsy
Identification of pathogenic variants in the ABCC6 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria (skin lesions, ocular findings, and/or histopathology)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Yellowish papular skin lesions with peau d’orange texture
searchTerms: yellow papules with orange peel texture
skin bumps with peau d’orange appearance

pathognomonic.symptomName: Calcification and fragmentation of elastic fibers in skin biopsy
searchTerms: broken and calcified elastic fibers in skin biopsy
fragmented and calcified skin elastic tissue
skin biopsy showing elastic fiber damage

common.symptomName: Skin laxity and wrinkling in flexural areas
searchTerms: loose and wrinkled skin in folds
wrinkling of skin in flexural regions

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances including decreased visual acuity
Intermittent claudication due to peripheral arterial disease
searchTerms: painful walking due to poor circulation
blood in stool from fragile vessels
high blood pressure from blood vessel problems
secondary hypertension due to vessel disease
stroke caused by hardened blood vessels
cerebral infarction due to vessel hardening

laboratory: Possible anemia secondary to gastrointestinal bleeding
imaging: CT or MRI showing vascular calcifications
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ABCC6 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating fragmented and calcified elastic fibers with von Kossa stain

distinguishingFeatures: No angioid streaks on ophthalmologic exam
Systemic connective tissue disorder with skeletal abnormalities
No characteristic skin papules or elastic fiber calcification

redFlags: Sudden visual loss due to choroidal neovascularization
Gastrointestinal hemorrhage causing anemia or hemodynamic instability
Early onset peripheral arterial disease or myocardial infarction
references: Neldner KH. Pseudoxanthoma elasticum. Clin Dermatol. 1988;6(1):1-159.
Le Saux O, Urban Z, Tschuch C, et al. Mutations in a gene encoding an ABC transporter cause pseudoxanthoma elasticum. Nat Genet. 2000;25(2):223-227.
Li Q, Uitto J. The mineralization phenotype in pseudoxanthoma elasticum: clues from mouse models. Biochim Biophys Acta. 2013;1832(7):1280-1287.
